WHO.wiki: A specialized agency of the United Nations responsible for international public health, issuing global alerts, tracking viral variants, and coordinating the Access to COVID-19 Tools (ACT) Accelerator.

CDC.definition: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
CDC.wiki: The national public health agency of the United States under the Department of Health and Human Services, providing clinical guidelines, infection control protocols, and epidemic monitoring.

PHEIC.definition: Public Health Emergency of International Concern
PHEIC.wiki: A formal declaration by the World Health Organization of an extraordinary event determined to constitute a public health risk to other states through the international spread of disease.

R0.wiki: An epidemiological metric representing the average number of secondary infections produced by a single infected individual in a completely susceptible population.

CFR.wiki: The proportion of people diagnosed with a specified disease who die from that disease, serving as a primary measure of disease severity and virulence.

mRNA.wiki: A modern genetic vaccine technology that instructs host cells to produce a harmless viral antigen protein, triggering a robust humoral and cellular immune response.

PPE.wiki: Specialized clothing and equipment—such as N95/FFP3 respirators, face shields, surgical gowns, and nitrile gloves—worn by healthcare workers to prevent pathogen transmission.

PCR.wiki: A molecular laboratory technique used to amplify specific viral RNA or DNA sequences, providing the gold standard in diagnostic accuracy for pathogen detection.

ICU.wiki: A specialized hospital department providing advanced critical care, mechanical ventilation, and continuous organ monitoring for life-threatening respiratory failure.

FDA.wiki: The federal agency of the United States Department of Health and Human Services responsible for approving and granting Emergency Use Authorizations (EUAs) for vaccines and therapeutics.

EMA.wiki: An agency of the European Union responsible for evaluating, supervising, and monitoring the safety of medicinal products and vaccines across EU member states.

CEPI.wiki: A global partnership between public, private, philanthropic, and civil organizations to finance and coordinate the rapid development of epidemic and pandemic vaccines.
